pages.title: The Cruel King
pages.content: Moses (pbuh) was a great Messenger of Allah. He lived in Egypt more than 3000 years ago. Pharaoh was the king of Egypt. He was an unfair and cruel ruler. He did not believe in Allah. He thought he was a god. There was a big group in Egypt: the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel were the children of Jacob (pbuh). Joseph (pbuh) was one of these children. Prophet Abraham (pbuh) was their grandfather. They believed in one Allah, like Prophet Abraham (pbuh). So, they did not think the king was a god. This group had more people than the Egyptians. The king feared that this crowd might take control of his kingdom. Because of his fear, he was rude to the Children of Israel. He made them unhappy. He forced them to do dangerous work for no money.

options: They refused to do the king’s dangerous and difficult work for no money at all.
They did not believe in one Allah, so the king did not trust them.
They had more people than the Egyptians, and he was afraid they might take his kingdom.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says: “This group had more people than the Egyptians. The king feared that this crowd might take control of his kingdom. Because of his fear, he was rude to the Children of Israel.”

languageFocusExercises.title: Was, Were or Believed?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which past word fits each sentence?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Pharaoh [blank] the king of Egypt. … The Children of Israel [blank] the children of Jacob (pbuh). … They [blank] in one Allah, like Prophet Abraham (pbuh).
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use was with one person (Pharaoh was …) and were with more than one person (They were …). We say believe in Allah, and the story is in the past, so it is believed in.

feedback.correct: Correct. Was for one person, were for a group, and believed in for faith.
feedback.incorrect: Look at Chapter 1 again. Is the subject one person or a group? Which verb goes with “in one Allah”?

errorItems.sentence: He did not believed in Allah.
So, they did not thought the king was a god.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After did not, use the base verb: did not believe, did not think. Did already shows the past, so the next verb does not change.

feedback.correct: Well done. After did not, the verb stays in the base form.
feedback.incorrect: Find the two sentences in Chapter 1. After did not, use the verb without -ed or a past form.

languageFocusExercises.title: Why Was the King Rude?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to make the sentence from Chapter 1.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where does “Because of his fear” go?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Because of + a noun (his fear) gives the reason. Here the reason comes first, then a comma, then the result: he was rude to the Children of Israel.

feedback.correct: Correct. The reason comes first, then the result.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 1. Start with the reason: Because of …

pages.title: The King’s Dream
pages.content: Years passed and many despotic kings ruled Egypt. One day the king had a dream. He saw a fire in his vision. The fire came from Jerusalem and burnt the houses of the Egyptians. But it did not harm any of the Children of Israel. The king woke up and called his helpers and magicians. He asked about the dream. They said, “A boy will be born from the Children of Israel and he will kill the Egyptians.” Then, the king told his soldiers, “Kill all the baby boys of the Children of Israel.” His soldiers entered the houses and searched the rooms. When they found baby boys, they killed them. All mothers, fathers, and sisters cried, but the soldiers had no kindness. They were unkind and heartless.

exercises.title: The Dream and the Order
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 2 in the right order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: The king saw a fire from Jerusalem in his dream.
The king called his helpers and magicians.
The magicians said, “A boy will be born from the Children of Israel …”
The king gave a cruel order to his soldiers.

exercises.explanation: First the king had a dream about a fire from Jerusalem. He woke up and called his helpers and magicians. They said, “A boy will be born from the Children of Israel …” Then the king gave his soldiers a cruel order about the baby boys.

feedback.correct: Great! The dream made the king afraid, and his fear led to a cruel order.
feedback.incorrect: Follow Chapter 2 step by step: The dream, the king’s question, the magicians’ answer, and then the king’s words to his soldiers.

languageFocusExercises.title: Past Verbs in the Story
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each past verb from Chapter 2 with its base form.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the base form of each past verb?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: These verbs are irregular: they do not take -ed in the past. The story uses the past form (had, saw, came, found, told) because the events are finished.

feedback.correct: Correct. You know the base form of each irregular past verb.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentence in Chapter 2 with each verb. What is the verb in the present? For example, “the king had a dream” → have.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Will Happen?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word for each sentence from Chapter 2.
languageFocusExercises.question: Is it about the past or the future?

formChoices.sentence: The fire came from Jerusalem and [choice] the houses of the Egyptians.
They said, “A boy [choice] be born from the Children of Israel …”
“… and he [choice] kill the Egyptians.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The dream is a finished event, so it uses the past: burnt. The helpers and magicians talk about the future, so they use will + base verb: will be born, will kill.

feedback.correct: Correct. Past for the dream, will for the prediction.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 2 again. Is it the dream (past) or what the helpers say will happen (future)?

languageFocusExercises.title: Put the Events in Order
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the sentences from Chapter 2 in story order.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: One day the king had a dream.
The king woke up and called his helpers and magicians.
The king asked about the dream.
Then, the king told his soldiers, “Kill all the baby boys of the Children of Israel.”
When the soldiers found baby boys, they killed them.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Past verbs tell the events in order. One day starts the event, Then shows the next step, and When joins two past actions: First they found, then they killed.

feedback.correct: Correct. You followed the events from the dream to the soldiers’ actions.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 2 again. Look for One day, Then and When to find the order.

languageFocusExercises.question: What will happen, and what should people do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use will + verb, one imperative and When + past..., past....

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Join two past actions: “When …, we …”

pages.title: A Baby in a Basket
pages.content: Moses was born in that year. His mother was afraid that soldiers could find her baby. So, she could not sleep at night. She did not know what to do. She asked Allah for help. Allah said to her, “Take a basket. Put your baby in the basket. Take the basket to the River Nile. Allah will protect him.” Moses’s mother put the baby Moses in a basket and took it to the river. She put the basket in the water. The water carried it away. Moses’s mother was very worried and told her daughter to follow the basket. Moses’s mother was so sad. But she knew that Allah was kinder to the baby Moses than she was. Allah was their Lord and also the Lord of the Nile.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-nile
A light container made of thin sticks, used to carry things.
To keep someone safe from danger.

hotspots.title: The Basket
hotspots.description: Allah told the mother of Moses (pbuh) to put her baby in a basket.

hotspots.title: The River Nile
hotspots.description: The water of the river carried the basket far away.

exercises.title: Trust in Allah
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 3.
exercises.question: Why did Moses’s mother put her baby in the River Nile?
options: The king’s soldiers told her to take the baby to the river.
Allah told her to do it and said He would protect the baby.
Queen Asiye asked her to send the baby to the palace.
exercises.explanation: Allah said to her, “Take a basket. Put your baby in the basket. Take the basket to the River Nile. Allah will protect him.” She was sad, “but she knew that Allah was kinder to the baby Moses than she was.”

feedback.correct: Right! She followed Allah’s words and trusted Him, even when she was sad and worried.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 3 again. Who spoke to Moses’s mother, and what did He say?

languageFocusExercises.title: Could or Could Not?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose could or could not for each sentence.
languageFocusExercises.question: Was something possible, or was she not able?

formChoices.sentence: His mother was afraid that soldiers [choice] find her baby.
So, she [choice] sleep at night.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Could + base verb can show that something was possible in the past: soldiers could find her baby (this was the danger). Could not + base verb shows that someone was not able to do something: she could not sleep.

feedback.correct: Correct. The danger was possible, so she was not able to sleep.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first sentences of Chapter 3. What was the mother afraid of? What happened at night because of this?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Did She Do?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did Moses’s mother do? What did the water do?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Moses’s mother [blank] the baby Moses in a basket and [blank] it to the river. … The water [blank] it away.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The story tells us what happened, so the verbs are in the past: put (put is the same in the present and the past), took (take → took) and carried (carry → carried). Allah’s words to Moses’s mother are read as they are; we do not change them.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the past forms that tell the story.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentences after Allah’s words in Chapter 3 again. What did Moses’s mother do? Use the past form.

languageFocusExercises.title: Told Her To … / Kinder Than
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the two sentences about Moses’s mother?

errorItems.sentence: Moses’s mother was very worried and told her daughter follow the basket.
But she knew that Allah was more kind to the baby Moses than she was.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Tell + person + to + base verb reports an instruction: told her daughter to follow. For a short adjective, add -er + than to compare: kind → kinder than.

feedback.correct: Well done. Told her daughter to follow, and kinder than.
feedback.incorrect: Find the two sentences near the end of Chapter 3. What word comes before follow? How do we compare with kind?

pages.title: The Queen’s Love
pages.content: Allah told the waves to be kind while carrying the baby. Soon, the basket came to the edge of the river. It was near the king’s palace. The palace servants saw the basket and took it to the king and the queen, Asiye. Queen Asiye saw the baby, and Allah placed a lot of love for him in her heart. The queen was different from her husband. She believed in Allah. She was good and kind-hearted. She told her husband, “I will take him to the palace and look after him.” The king accepted. She said to her servants, “Find a nurse for the baby.” Moses’s sister saw everything. She ran to the queen and said, “I know a good woman. She lives nearby. She will be a good nurse for the baby.”

vocabulary.definition: A very large house where a king or queen lives.
People who work in someone else’s house.
Gentle and caring towards other people.
A woman who feeds and cares for a baby.

hotspots.title: Queen Asiye
hotspots.description: Allah put a lot of love for baby Moses (pbuh) in the heart of Queen Asiye.

hotspots.title: The King’s Palace
hotspots.description: The basket came to the edge of the river near the king’s palace.

exercises.title: Who Did What?
exercises.instructions: Match each person with what they did in Chapter 4.
exercises.question: Who did what in Chapter 4?

matchingPairs.right: saw the basket by the water and took it
said she would take baby Moses to the palace and look after him
said she knew a good woman to nurse the baby

correctAnswer.The servants: saw the basket by the water and took it
correctAnswer.Queen Asiye: said she would take baby Moses to the palace and look after him
correctAnswer.Moses’s sister: said she knew a good woman to nurse the baby

exercises.explanation: The palace servants saw the basket and took it to the king and the queen. Queen Asiye said, “I will take him to the palace and look after him.” “The king accepted.” Moses’s sister ran to the queen and said, “I know a good woman … She will be a good nurse for the baby.”

feedback.correct: Well done! Asiye’s kind heart and the sister’s quick help kept baby Moses safe.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 4 again and find each person: The servants at the start, then the queen and the king, and Moses’s sister at the end.

languageFocusExercises.title: Going Somewhere or Being Somewhere?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each part of Chapter 4 in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Going to a place, or where something is?

dragDropGroups.group: Going to a place or person
items: Soon, the basket came to the edge of the river.
The palace servants saw the basket and took it to the king and the queen
She ran to the queen
It was near the king’s palace.
She lives nearby.

Going to a place or person: Soon, the basket came to the edge of the river.
The palace servants saw the basket and took it to the king and the queen
Where something is: It was near the king’s palace.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: A movement verb + to shows where someone or something goes: came to, took it to, ran to. Near and nearby say where something is. The sister says “She lives nearby” in the present because the woman still lives there when she speaks.

feedback.correct: Correct. To + place shows movement; near and nearby show position.
feedback.incorrect: Look for a movement verb + to. Near and nearby tell us where something is.

languageFocusExercises.title: Words About the Queen
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word from Chapter 4 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 4 mean?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The queen was different from her husband: She was not like him. She believed in Allah and was kind-hearted. Remember: we say different from, not different than or different of.

feedback.correct: Correct. These words help us describe the queen and what happened.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentences about Queen Asiye in Chapter 4 again. What did the king do when she asked to keep the baby?

languageFocusExercises.title: A Decision and an Order
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word for each sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word shows a decision, and which word gives an order?

formChoices.sentence: She told her husband, “I [choice] take him to the palace and look after him.”
She said to her servants, “[choice] a nurse for the baby.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: I will + base verb shows a decision the speaker makes now. An order starts with the base verb and has no subject: Find a nurse.

feedback.correct: Correct. Will for the queen’s decision, the base verb for her order.
feedback.incorrect: Read what the queen says to her husband and to her servants in Chapter 4.

pages.title: Back to His Mother
pages.content: Moses’s sister brought her mother to the palace to take care of the baby. Allah sent Moses back to his mother. Baby Moses was in his mother’s arms again. His mother looked after baby Moses. Allah is the Best Protector. Queen Asiye loved Moses so much. Moses grew up in a safe place, in the house of the king. He always loved Allah. He knew that the king was not a god. Years passed and Moses became a strong young man. He was always ready to help the weak people. He loved the Children of Israel because his mother was from the Children of Israel. One day he was walking in the bazaar. He saw two men fighting. One of them was an Egyptian.

hotspots.title: His Mother’s Arms
hotspots.description: Allah sent baby Moses (pbuh) back to his mother’s arms.

exercises.title: Moses and His People
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 5.
exercises.question: Moses grew up in the king’s house. Why did he love the Children of Israel?
options: Queen Asiye was from the Children of Israel.
The king asked him to help them.
His mother was from the Children of Israel.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5 says: “He loved the Children of Israel because his mother was from the Children of Israel.” Allah had sent Moses back to his mother, and she looked after him.

feedback.correct: Yes! His own mother was from the Children of Israel, so he loved them and was ready to help the weak.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 5 again. Find the sentence about the Children of Israel with the word “because”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Care and Change
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word from Chapter 5 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 5 mean?

matchingPairs.right: people with little power or strength

correctAnswer.the weak people: people with little power or strength

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Take care of and look after have the same meaning; the chapter uses both. Grew up and became show change over time: Moses grew up in a safe place and became a strong young man.

feedback.correct: Correct. You found words for care and for change.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 5 again. Which two phrases does the chapter use for the mother’s care?

languageFocusExercises.title: Always and Because
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word means “all the time”, and which gives a reason?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Moses grew up in a safe place, in the house of the king. He [blank] loved Allah. … He loved the Children of Israel [blank] his mother was from the Children of Israel.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Always shows that something was true all the time. Because + subject + verb gives a reason (because his mother was …). Because of goes before a noun only, for example because of his fear.

feedback.correct: Correct. Always for something true all the time, because for the reason.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 5 again. Did Moses love Allah all the time? After the second blank there is a subject and a verb (his mother was).

languageFocusExercises.title: Walking, Then Seeing
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentences from Chapter 5. True or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “One day he was walking in the bazaar. He saw two men fighting.” — Moses started walking after he saw the two men.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Was walking (was + -ing) shows an action that was already happening. Saw (simple past) shows a new event in the middle of that action. So Moses was walking first, and then he saw the men.

feedback.correct: Correct. The walking was already happening when he saw the men.
feedback.incorrect: Look again: was walking describes an action in progress. The new event, saw, happened during the walk.

pages.title: A Mistake in the Bazaar
pages.content: The other man was from the Children of Israel. Suddenly, the poor and weak man from the Children of Israel shouted, “Help me!” Moses ran to help him. He hit the Egyptian and the man died there. Moses was very upset. He was so sorry because he accidentally caused someone’s death. He made dua to Allah, “Forgive me. I accidentally caused someone’s death.” Allah forgave him because He is Kind and Loving. A man from the city came and said to him, “The king’s soldiers are looking for you. You killed an Egyptian. Now they are going to catch you. Run away from the city. Soldiers of the king will kill you.”

__historical_entity__:moses-ancient-egyptians

exercises.title: A Mistake
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 6.
exercises.question: Moses caused the man’s death by accident.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says Moses was very sorry “because he accidentally caused someone’s death.” He made dua: “Forgive me.” Allah forgave him.

feedback.correct: Correct! It was an accident. Moses was sorry and asked Allah to forgive him.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 6 again. Find the word that tells us how it happened, and see how Moses felt.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Accidentally” Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 6. Choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: “He was so sorry because he accidentally caused someone’s death.” What does accidentally tell us?
options: He wanted to do it and planned it.
He did not plan to do it.
He did it many times before that.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Accidentally means not on purpose: Moses did not plan or want this result. That is why he was so sorry and asked Allah to forgive him.

feedback.correct: Correct. Accidentally means he did not plan it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Why? — To … / Because …
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 6.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words tell us why something happened?

formChoices.sentence: Moses ran [choice] him.
Allah forgave him [choice] He is Kind and Loving.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: To + base verb gives the purpose of an action: Moses ran to help him. Because + subject + verb gives a reason: because He is Kind and Loving.

feedback.correct: Correct. To help gives the purpose, because gives the reason.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 6 again. Why did Moses run? Why did Allah forgive him?

languageFocusExercises.title: A Friend’s Warning
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the verbs about now and about the future?

errorItems.sentence: “The king’s soldiers are look for you. You killed an Egyptian.”
“Now they are going catch you. Run away from the city.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Are + verb-ing shows what is happening now: are looking for you. Are going to + base verb shows what the man expects will happen soon: are going to catch you.

feedback.correct: Well done. Are looking for now, are going to catch for the future.
feedback.incorrect: Read the man’s words at the end of Chapter 6. Be + -ing for now; be going to + base verb for the future.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use to + verb, because, present continuous, be going to/will and an imperative.

pages.title: Escape to Midian
pages.content: Moses knew that the penalty for killing an Egyptian was death. Moses escaped from the soldiers. He left Egypt and traveled for a long time. He was not alone. Allah guided him. After many days, he arrived at Midian. Midian was near Egypt. The king of Egypt was not the ruler there. Moses was tired and thirsty. So, he looked for water. Soon, he found a well. There were many men around the water. These were shepherds with their sheep. They were watering their animals. Two girls were sitting far from the water. They also had sheep with them. But they did not go near the well. Moses asked the girls, “Why are you sitting far away from the well?”

__historical_entity__:moses-midian

exercises.title: A Safe Place
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 7.
exercises.question: Why was Midian a safe place for Moses?
options: It had high walls and many strong soldiers.
The king of Egypt was not the ruler there.
His mother and sister lived there with their family.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7 says: “Midian was near Egypt. The king of Egypt was not the ruler there.” So Moses was safe from the king in Midian.

feedback.correct: Right! Midian was near Egypt, but the king of Egypt did not rule there.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentences about Midian in the middle of Chapter 7. Was it far from Egypt? Who ruled there?

languageFocusExercises.title: At the Well
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word for each sentence from Chapter 7.
languageFocusExercises.question: Is it one, or more than one? Which word fits?

formChoices.sentence: There [choice] many men around the water.
They [choice] watering their animals.
Two girls [choice] sitting far from the water.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: There were + plural noun tells us what was in a place. Were + verb-ing (were watering, were sitting) describes what people were doing at that moment in the past. Use were, not was, with more than one person.

feedback.correct: Correct. You used were with more than one person.
feedback.incorrect: Read the well scene in Chapter 7. Many men, they and two girls are more than one person.

languageFocusExercises.title: Arriving and Looking
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which small words fit the sentences?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: After many days, he arrived [blank] Midian. … Moses was tired and thirsty. [blank], he looked [blank] water.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: We say arrive at a place, not arrive to. So introduces the result: He was thirsty, so he looked for water. Look for means try to find.

feedback.correct: Correct. Arrived at, So, and looked for.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 7 again. What did Moses do because he was thirsty? Which word goes after arrived?

languageFocusExercises.title: Journey Words
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word from Chapter 7 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 7 mean?

matchingPairs.right: a deep hole in the ground with water

correctAnswer.a well: a deep hole in the ground with water

languageFocusExercises.explanation: These words help us follow Moses’s journey: he escaped from the soldiers, Allah guided him, and he was thirsty when he found a well with shepherds.

feedback.correct: Correct. You know the key words of the journey.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 7 again. Find each word and look at the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use after, arrived at, so, looked for, there were and was/were + -ing.

feedback.correct: Use the forms in a new situation.

pages.title: The Two Sisters
pages.content: Moses asked them, “Why aren’t you taking your sheep to drink water?” The girls said, “Our father is very old. He cannot come with us. There are no young men in our house to help us. So, we take the sheep to the water. We wait for our turn.” Moses understood that the two sisters needed help. He took their sheep to the water and gave them a drink. The girls were very happy. They took their sheep and went home. When the sisters came home early, their father asked, “What happened? You came home very early!” The sisters said, “A young man helped us to water our sheep. We did not wait for the other shepherds to leave the well.”

vocabulary.definition: The time when it is your chance to do something.
Knew or saw clearly what something meant.
Before the usual time.
People whose job is to look after sheep.

hotspots.title: Waiting for Their Turn
hotspots.description: The sisters waited because their father was old and no young men could help them.

hotspots.title: Water for the Sheep
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) took the sisters’ sheep to the water and gave them a drink.

exercises.title: Help at the Well
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 8 in the right order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: The girls said, “Our father is very old.”
Moses took their sheep to the water.
The girls went home early.
The girls’ father asked, “What happened?”

exercises.explanation: At the well, the girls explained that their father was very old. Moses understood that they needed help and took their sheep to the water. The girls went home early, and their father asked, “What happened? You came home very early!”

feedback.correct: Well done! Moses saw that the sisters needed help, and he helped them at once.
feedback.incorrect: Follow Chapter 8 from the girls’ answer at the well, to Moses’s help, to the girls’ return home.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Cannot” Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the girls’ words. Choose the best meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Our father is very old. He cannot come with us.” What does cannot come tell us?
options: He does not want to come.
He is not able to come.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Cannot + base verb means someone is not able to do something now. Their father is very old, so he is not able to come to the well.

feedback.correct: Correct. Cannot means he is not able.
feedback.incorrect: Read the girls’ answer in Chapter 8 again. Why can their father not come?

languageFocusExercises.title: Build Moses’s Question
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to build Moses’s question from Chapter 8.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where do aren’t and you go in a Why question?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: In a question, the helping verb comes before the subject: Why + aren’t + you + verb-ing …? This question asks why an action is not happening now.

feedback.correct: Correct. Why + aren’t + you + taking …?
feedback.incorrect: Read the first line of Chapter 8. In a question, aren’t comes before you.

languageFocusExercises.title: Fix the Sisters’ Words
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the sisters’ words?

errorItems.sentence: “There is no young men in our house to help us. So, we take the sheep to the water.”
“We did not wait for the other shepherds leave the well.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: There are no + plural noun says that something is not there: There are no young men. Wait for + person + to + base verb: wait for the other shepherds to leave.

feedback.correct: Well done. There are no young men, and wait for the shepherds to leave.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sisters’ words in Chapter 8. Young men is plural. What small word comes before leave?

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: Explain a Shared Task
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about a job you share at home.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who helps at home, and who cannot?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use Why aren’t you...?, cannot, There are no..., so, wait for, when or early.

feedback.correct: Keep the example new and clear.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Ask a question: “Why aren’t you …?”
discussionPrompts.example: Why aren’t you helping us with the dishes?

beforeYouRead.quote: There are no young men in our house to help us.

pages.title: A New Life
pages.content: The father of these girls was Prophet Shu’ayb (pbuh). Shu’ayb (pbuh) was a Messenger of Allah in Midian. He was very old, so he couldn’t help his daughters. Shu’ayb (pbuh) said, “Go and call the young man. I want to thank him for his work.” Moses came to the house. He ate food with the girls’ father. Shu’ayb (pbuh) offered Moses a job. Moses accepted the job because he was a stranger in Midian. He needed a job and a house. Moses began to stay with the family. He helped them in their work. Later, he married one of the sisters. They lived a happy life. After ten years, Moses decided to go back to Egypt.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-egypt-ancient
__historical_entity__:moses-midian
Said that you would give something to someone if they wanted it.

hotspots.title: Prophet Shu’ayb
hotspots.description: Prophet Shu’ayb (pbuh), the sisters’ father, offered Moses (pbuh) a job in Midian.

hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) stayed with the family, and later he married one of the sisters.

exercises.title: A New Life
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 9.
exercises.question: Why did Moses accept Shu’ayb’s (pbuh) offer?
options: He was a stranger in Midian and needed a job and a house.
He wanted to live in the king’s palace again.
The shepherds at the well asked him to stay in Midian.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 9 says: “Moses accepted the job because he was a stranger in Midian. He needed a job and a house.”

feedback.correct: Yes! He was a stranger with no job and no home, so Shu’ayb’s (pbuh) offer helped him.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 9 again. Find the sentence with “Moses accepted …” and read to the end of the next sentence.

languageFocusExercises.title: Couldn’t, Needed, Because
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: He was very old, so he [blank] help his daughters. … Moses accepted the job [blank] he was a stranger in Midian. He [blank] a job and a house.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Couldn’t + base verb means he was not able in the past. Because gives the reason for Moses’s choice. Needed + noun says what was necessary for him.

feedback.correct: Correct. Couldn’t, because and needed each do a different job.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 9 again. The story is in the past. Why did Moses accept the job?

languageFocusExercises.title: Want To, Decided To
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 9.
languageFocusExercises.question: What comes after “want” and “decided”?

formChoices.sentence: Shu’ayb (pbuh) said, “Go and call the young man. I want [choice] him for his work.”
After ten years, Moses decided [choice] back to Egypt.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Want to + base verb shows what someone wishes to do. Decided to + base verb shows a choice about the future.

feedback.correct: Correct. Want to thank and decided to go.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 9 again. After want and decided, use to + base verb.

languageFocusExercises.title: Moses’s New Life
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the sentences from Chapter 9 in story order.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which time words help you find the order?

sequencingItems.text: Moses came to the house.
Shu’ayb (pbuh) offered Moses a job.
Later, Moses married one of the sisters.
After ten years, Moses decided …

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Later and After ten years move the story forward in time. They help the reader follow a long period of Moses’s life.

feedback.correct: Correct. Later and After ten years show the order.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 9 again. Look for Later and After ten years.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: A New Opportunity
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about a new plan for your class.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do you need, and what will you do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use need, because, want to, offer/accept, later, after + time or decide to.

feedback.correct: Use the forms in a new situation.

discussionPrompts.example: We need it because we have many new books.

discussionPrompts.example: Later, we decided to open the corner on Monday.

pages.title: The Voice on the Mountain
pages.content: He took his family. They started to travel to Egypt. They traveled a long time. It was winter. There was nobody on the way. It was getting dark and cold. They were in a valley between mountains. Suddenly, Moses saw a fire on the hillside. He said to his family, “Wait here. I will get some fire to get warm.” Moses climbed the mountain. It was already dark. Everywhere was very quiet. In the silence, he heard a loud voice: “Moses, I am Allah. I chose you. Listen to me. There is no god but Me.” Then Allah told Moses, “Put down your walking stick!” Moses put down his walking stick on the ground. It turned into a big snake!

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-egypt-ancient
__historical_entity__:moses-mount-sinai
__historical_entity__:moses-valley-of-tuwa
The side of a small mountain, going up or down.
Complete quiet, with no sound.
A long, thin piece of wood that you hold and lean on.

hotspots.title: Fire on the Hillside
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) saw a fire on the hillside and climbed the mountain.

hotspots.title: The Walking Stick
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) put down his walking stick, and it turned into a big snake.

exercises.title: The Fire on the Hill
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 10.
exercises.question: Why did Moses go up the mountain?
options: He heard a voice on the mountain.
He was looking for water for his family.
He wanted to get some fire to get warm.
exercises.explanation: It was dark and cold. Moses saw a fire on the hillside and said, “Wait here. I will get some fire to get warm.” He heard the voice later, when he was on the mountain.

feedback.correct: Right! It was dark and cold, so Moses went to get fire. There, Allah spoke to him.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 10 again. What did Moses say to his family before he climbed?

languageFocusExercises.title: It or There?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word for each sentence from Chapter 10.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words fit the weather, the time and the empty road?

formChoices.sentence: [choice] was winter.
[choice] was nobody on the way.
It was [choice] dark and cold.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use It was for the season, the weather or the time: It was winter. Use There was to say if something or someone is in a place: There was nobody on the way. It was getting + adjective shows a slow change: It was getting dark.

feedback.correct: Correct. It for the season, There for nobody on the way, and getting for a slow change.
feedback.incorrect: Read the start of Chapter 10 again. Is the sentence about the season, or about people on the way?

languageFocusExercises.title: Moses’s Plan
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to build Moses’s words to his family.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where does the reason (to get warm) go?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Wait here is an instruction. I will + base verb gives Moses’s plan. To + base verb at the end gives the purpose: to get warm.

feedback.correct: Correct. An instruction, a plan with will, and the purpose with to.
feedback.incorrect: Read what Moses says to his family in Chapter 10. Start with the instruction.

languageFocusExercises.title: Words from the Mountain
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word from Chapter 10 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 10 mean?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Turn into + noun shows a change from one thing to another: The walking stick turned into a big snake. Suddenly shows that something happens with no warning.

feedback.correct: Correct. You know the key words of the scene on the mountain.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 10 again. Find each word and look at the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: A Cold Evening
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about a cold evening.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is changing, and what will you do?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use getting + adjective, there is/are, an imperative, will + verb, and to + verb.

feedback.correct: Keep the situation new.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say how it is changing: “It was getting …”
discussionPrompts.example: It was getting dark and cold in the park.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Tell someone what to do: “Put on …, please.”
discussionPrompts.example: Put on your jacket, please.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what you will do: “I will …”
discussionPrompts.example: I will make some hot tea at home.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say why: “We will … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: We will drink it to get warm.

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. What was the weather like on the way?
options: It was a hot summer day.
It was winter, dark and cold.

iCan: I can tell what happened on the mountain.
I can say what I will do and why.
I can describe a cold evening.

pages.title: The Signs of Allah
pages.content: Allah spoke to Moses again, “Put your hand inside your clothes. Now take it out. See, your hand is now shining.” Allah said, “I am showing you the signs of My power. Go to the king and tell him Allah is the most powerful.” After this message from Allah, Moses became a Messenger of Allah, a prophet. Moses (pbuh) went to Egypt. He met the king and his helpers. But they did not believe in Allah. Allah chose Moses and made him His prophet. Moses (pbuh) took his brother Harun (pbuh) with him and went to the palace to give the message of Allah. The king was sitting on his throne. His helpers and soldiers were standing around him.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-egypt-ancient
__historical_entity__:moses-pharaohs-palace
Giving out bright light.
Things that show the power of Allah.
A person chosen by Allah to guide people.
A special chair for a king or queen.

hotspots.title: The Shining Hand
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) took out his hand, and it was shining. It was a sign of Allah’s power.

hotspots.title: Harun
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) took his brother Harun (pbuh) with him to give Allah’s message to the king.

exercises.title: Ready for the Mission
exercises.instructions: Match each part with what Chapter 11 says about it.
exercises.question: What does Chapter 11 tell us?

matchingPairs.right: Moses’s brother, who went with him

correctAnswer.Harun: Moses’s brother, who went with him

exercises.explanation: Allah said, “I am showing you the signs of My power. Go to the king and tell him Allah is the most powerful.” Moses took his brother Harun with him to the palace, where “the king was sitting on his throne.”

feedback.correct: Great! You found the sign, the helper, the king and the message.
feedback.incorrect: The beginning of Chapter 11 is about the hand and the message. The end is about Harun and the king in the palace.

languageFocusExercises.title: An Instruction or a Story Event?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each part of Chapter 11 in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Is it an order to Moses, or something that happened?

dragDropGroups.group: Allah tells Moses what to do
items: Put your hand inside your clothes.
Now take it out.
Go to the king
Moses (pbuh) went to Egypt.
Moses met the king and his helpers.
The king was sitting on his throne.

Allah tells Moses what to do: Put your hand inside your clothes.
The story tells what happened: Moses met the king and his helpers.
The king was sitting on his throne.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: An instruction starts with the base verb and has no subject: Put …, Take …, Go …. The story events have a subject and a past verb: Moses went, He met, The king was sitting.

feedback.correct: Correct. Base verb with no subject = instruction; subject + past verb = story event.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the first word. Is it a base verb with no subject, or a subject and a past verb?

languageFocusExercises.title: A New Role
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word for each sentence from Chapter 11.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which past forms complete the sentences?

formChoices.sentence: After this message from Allah, Moses [choice] a Messenger of Allah, a prophet.
But they [choice] believe in Allah.
Allah chose Moses and [choice] him His prophet.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Became + noun shows a change into a new role. Did not + base verb makes a past negative. Made + person + noun also shows a new role: Made him His prophet.

feedback.correct: Correct. Became, did not and made are all past forms.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 11 again. The story is in the past.

languageFocusExercises.title: With Whom? Why?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who went with Moses, and why did he go?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Moses (pbuh) took his brother Harun (pbuh) [blank] him and went to the palace [blank] give the message of Allah.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Take + person + with + me/him shows who goes together. To + base verb gives the purpose: to give the message.

feedback.correct: Correct. With Harun, and to give the message.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 11 again. Before a base verb (give), use to for the purpose.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: A Small Mission
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about a small job you did.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you tell us about a small job?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use an imperative, take + person + with, go to + place, to + verb, become, or make + person + complement.

feedback.correct: Use a new everyday task.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what someone asked: “Take this … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: Take this note to the school office, please.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say who went with you: “I took … with me.”
discussionPrompts.example: I took my friend Sami with me.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say why you went: “We went to … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: We went to the office to give the note to the secretary.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say how things changed: “After that, I became …”
discussionPrompts.example: After that day, I became the class helper.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did Moses (pbuh) become after this message?
beforeYouRead.quote: After this message from Allah, Moses became a Messenger of Allah, a prophet.

iCan: I can say what the signs of Allah were.
I can say who went with me and why.
I can tell about a small job I did.

groupTask.title: From Egypt to the Mountain

roles.name: Reader A (Egypt)
roles.job: You know Chapters 6–7: why Moses had to leave Egypt and how he traveled.

roles.name: Reader B (Midian)
roles.job: You know Chapters 7–9: the well, the two sisters and the ten years in Midian.

roles.name: Reader C (The Mountain)
roles.job: You know Chapters 10–11: the fire, the voice on the mountain and the way back to Egypt.

roles.name: Map Keeper
roles.job: You ask questions, draw the route on paper and write one reason next to each place.

steps: Each reader reads only his or her chapters and then closes the book.
The Map Keeper asks each reader: Where did he go? Why did he go there? How long did he stay?

Each reader answers with one sentence from the book, for example: “He left Egypt and traveled for a long time.” or “After ten years, Moses decided to go back to Egypt.” The Map Keeper adds the place and the reason to the route.
Together, check your route on the map page Moses’s Journey in the app and correct any mistakes.
groupTask.share: Each group shows its route to the class and gives one reason for each move: “He went to … because …”.
groupTask.solo: Cover Chapters 6–11 and draw the route Egypt → Midian → the mountain → Egypt from memory. Write one reason for each move, then check it on the map page Moses’s Journey.

pages.title: The King’s Magicians
pages.content: Moses (pbuh) told him about Allah. He said to him, “I am the Messenger from the Lord of the universe.” The king listened to Moses (pbuh). He thought Moses was crazy. Moses (pbuh) decided to show the miracles. Moses (pbuh) took his walking stick and threw it on the ground. The stick turned into a big snake! Then he put his hand inside his clothes. He took his hand out. Look! It was shining white! These were miracles of Allah. Allah gave them to Moses (pbuh) to help him. The king and his helpers laughed at him. He made fun of Moses and his message. The king said to Moses (pbuh), “This is only magic. All of my magicians can do this.”

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-pharaohs-magicians
Everything that exists: the earth, the sky and space.
Mad; not able to think in a normal way.
Made a choice after thinking.
Made fun of someone.

hotspots.title: Two Miracles
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) showed the king two miracles: The big snake and the shining white hand.

hotspots.title: The King Laughed
hotspots.description: The king and his helpers laughed at Moses (pbuh). The king said the miracles were only magic.

exercises.title: Miracle or Magic?
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 12.
exercises.question: The king said that Moses’s signs were miracles from Allah.
exercises.explanation: The story calls the signs “miracles of Allah”, but the king and his helpers laughed. The king said, “This is only magic. All of my magicians can do this.”

feedback.correct: Correct! The king did not accept the miracles. He called them “only magic”.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 12 again. What did the king say to Moses (pbuh)?

languageFocusExercises.title: Words in the Palace
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word from Chapter 12 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 12 mean?

matchingPairs.right: not thinking in a normal way

correctAnswer.crazy: not thinking in a normal way

languageFocusExercises.explanation: He thought Moses was crazy: thought + sentence tells us the king’s opinion, not a fact. The chapter shows he was wrong: The stick and the shining hand were miracles of Allah.

feedback.correct: Correct. You know the key words of the palace scene.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 12 again. Find each word and look at the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Told, Decided To, Can
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 12.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words fit the sentences?

formChoices.sentence: Moses (pbuh) [choice] him about Allah.
Moses (pbuh) decided [choice] the miracles.
“This is only magic. All of my magicians can [choice] this.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Tell + person + about: told him about Allah (said does not take a person directly). Decided to + base verb shows a choice. Can + base verb (with no to) shows ability.

feedback.correct: Correct. Told him about, decided to show, can do.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 12 again. Which verb can have “him” right after it? What comes after can?

languageFocusExercises.title: The Signs, Step by Step
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the sentences from Chapter 12 in story order.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word shows the next step?

sequencingItems.text: Moses (pbuh) took his walking stick and threw it on the ground.
The stick turned into a big snake!
Then Moses put his hand inside his clothes.
Moses took his hand out.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Past verbs give the actions in order. Then shows the next step: After the stick, Moses showed the second sign.

feedback.correct: Correct. First the stick, then the hand.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 12 again. Look for Then to find the second sign.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: Show and Explain
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about something you can make.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you show someone how you make something?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use thought + clause, decided to, turned into, then, to + verb or can + verb.

feedback.correct: Keep the example new and simple.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what someone thought: “My friend thought …, so I decided to …”
discussionPrompts.example: My friend thought my paper boat could not float, so I decided to show him.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say how it changed: “It turned into …”
discussionPrompts.example: I folded the flat paper, and it turned into a small boat.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say why you did it: “I … to …”
discussionPrompts.example: I put it in the water to test it.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what you can do now: “Now I can …”
discussionPrompts.example: Now I can make a paper boat in two minutes.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did the king and his helpers do?
beforeYouRead.quote: The king and his helpers laughed at him.

iCan: I can tell what the king said about the miracles.
I can say how something changed.
I can show and explain a simple skill.

pages.title: The Magicians Believe
pages.content: He invited his magicians to the palace. The magicians came with sticks in their hands. Some were holding ropes. They put down the sticks and ropes on the ground. They were moving like snakes! Then, Allah spoke to Moses (pbuh), “Throw your stick!” Moses (pbuh) threw down his stick and it turned into a huge snake. His stick quickly ate all the snakes of the magicians. The magicians bowed down to Allah. They shouted, “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!” The king still did not believe in Allah because he was arrogant. The king did not like those people because they believed in Allah. He continued to harm Moses (pbuh) and his people day and night.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-pharaohs-palace
__historical_entity__:moses-pharaohs-magicians
Thick, strong pieces of string used to tie things.
Very big.
Put the head down low to worship Allah.
Thinking you are better than other people.

hotspots.title: The Huge Snake
hotspots.description: The stick of Moses (pbuh) turned into a huge snake and ate all the snakes of the magicians.

hotspots.title: Bowing Down
hotspots.description: The magicians bowed down to Allah and believed in the Lord of Moses and Harun (pbuh).

exercises.title: The Magicians Believe
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 13 in the right order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: The magicians put down their sticks and ropes.
Allah said to Moses (pbuh), “Throw your stick!”
Moses’s stick ate all the snakes of the magicians.
The magicians shouted, “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!”

exercises.explanation: The magicians put their sticks and ropes on the ground. Allah told Moses, “Throw your stick!” His stick turned into a huge snake and ate all the magicians’ snakes. Then the magicians bowed down and shouted, “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!”

feedback.correct: Great! The magicians saw the truth and changed their minds. But the arrogant king still did not believe.
feedback.incorrect: Follow Chapter 13 step by step: The magicians’ sticks, Allah’s words, what Moses’s stick did, and what the magicians shouted.

languageFocusExercises.title: Finished or in Progress?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each part of Chapter 13 in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Did it happen once, or was it going on?

items: The magicians came with sticks in their hands.
They put down the sticks and ropes on the ground.
The magicians bowed down to Allah.
Some were holding ropes.
They were moving like snakes!

A finished action: The magicians came with sticks in their hands.
They put down the sticks and ropes on the ground.
The magicians bowed down to Allah.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The simple past (came, put down, bowed down) tells a finished action. Was/were + verb-ing (were holding, were moving) shows an action in progress at that moment, like a picture of the scene.

feedback.correct: Correct. Simple past for finished actions, were + -ing for actions in progress.
feedback.incorrect: Look for were + -ing. Those actions were in progress.

languageFocusExercises.title: Fix the Past Verb and the Adverb
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct word.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the two words about Moses’s stick?

errorItems.sentence: Moses (pbuh) throwed down his stick and it turned into a huge snake.
His stick quick ate all the snakes of the magicians.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Throw is irregular: throw → threw. To describe how an action happens, use an adverb (often adjective + -ly): quick → quickly.

feedback.correct: Well done. Threw and quickly.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 13 again. Throw has an irregular past. Which word tells us how the stick ate?

languageFocusExercises.title: Still, Because, Continued To
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: The king [blank] did not believe in Allah, [blank] he was arrogant. … He continued [blank] harm Moses (pbuh) and his people day and night.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Still + did not shows that the situation did not change, even after the miracle. Because gives the reason. Continued to + base verb means he did not stop.

feedback.correct: Correct. Still, because and continued to.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 13 again. Did the king change after the miracle? Why not?

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: A Small Demonstration
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about a small experiment.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you say how something changed?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use came with, was/were + -ing, an imperative, turned into, quickly, because, still or continued to.

feedback.correct: Use a new everyday situation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say who came and what they had: “… came with …”
discussionPrompts.example: My cousin came with a bag of seeds. She was holding a small pot too.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Tell someone what to do: “Put …”
discussionPrompts.example: Put the seeds in the soil.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say how it changed: “After …, … turned into …”
discussionPrompts.example: After two weeks, the seeds turned into small green plants.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what still happens and why: “She/He still … because …”
discussionPrompts.example: My cousin still waters them every day because she loves her plants.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Where did the king invite his magicians?
beforeYouRead.quote: He invited his magicians to the palace.

iCan: I can tell how the magicians came to believe.
I can say why someone still did something.
I can describe a small experiment.

pages.title: The Night Journey
pages.content: He told his helpers and soldiers, “Be rude to them!” Life became harder for them. Moses (pbuh) asked Allah for help. And Allah told him, “Travel with your people at night.” Moses (pbuh) called his people and said, “Get ready for the journey. We are going away from Egypt. But you must keep it secret. We must hide it. We will leave at night.” They left Egypt at night. There was a large group with many old people and children. The children and the old could not walk fast and got tired very quickly. Their caravan moved slowly. When the sun rose, they arrived at the sea. The king prepared his huge army.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:moses-egypt-ancient
__historical_entity__:moses-red-sea
A trip from one place to another.
Known only by a few people and hidden from others.
A group of people traveling together.
A large group of soldiers.

hotspots.title: Leaving at Night
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) and his people left Egypt secretly at night.

hotspots.title: The Caravan
hotspots.description: The caravan moved slowly because there were many old people and children.

exercises.title: A Slow Caravan
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 14.
exercises.question: Why did the caravan move slowly?
options: It was a dark night, and they could not see the road very well.
There were many old people and children, and they could not walk fast.
They were waiting for the king’s army to leave the city first.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 14 says: “There was a large group with many old people and children. The children and the old could not walk fast and got tired very quickly. Their caravan moved slowly.”

feedback.correct: Right! The old people and children got tired quickly, so the whole group moved slowly.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 14 again. Look at the sentences just before “Their caravan moved slowly.”

languageFocusExercises.title: A Plan for the Journey
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read Moses’s words. True or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: Moses (pbuh) called his people and said, “Get ready for the journey. We are going away from Egypt.” — When Moses said this, the people were already far away from Egypt.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Get ready for is an instruction to prepare. We are going away (are + -ing) talks about a plan for the near future. The people had not left yet; they left Egypt at night.

feedback.correct: Correct. It was a plan: They were getting ready to leave.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 14 again. When did they leave Egypt? Get ready shows they had not left yet.

languageFocusExercises.title: Night Journey Words
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word from Chapter 14 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 14 mean?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: You must keep it secret: must + base verb shows that something is necessary. The people had to tell nobody about the journey.

feedback.correct: Correct. You know the key words of the night journey.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 14 again. Find each word and look at the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Slowly Through the Night
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct words for each sentence from Chapter 14.
languageFocusExercises.question: How did they move, and when did they arrive?

formChoices.sentence: The children and the old [choice] walk fast and got tired very quickly.
Their caravan moved [choice].
[choice] the sun rose, they arrived at the sea.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Could not + base verb shows past inability. An adverb (slow + -ly) tells us how the caravan moved. When + past links two past events that happen at the same time.

feedback.correct: Correct. Could not, slowly and When.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 14 again. The story is in the past. Which word tells us how the caravan moved?

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: Plan a Quiet Trip
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about a school trip.
languageFocusExercises.question: What must everyone do on the trip?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use an imperative, get ready for, must, will, could not, slowly/quickly or when.

feedback.correct: Use a new travel situation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Tell people to get ready: “Get ready for …”
discussionPrompts.example: Get ready for the school trip. Bring water and a hat.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what we must do: “We must …”
discussionPrompts.example: We must stay together on the bus.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say what will happen: “We will …”
discussionPrompts.example: We will leave at eight o’clock in the morning.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say who is slow: “… cannot walk fast, so …”
discussionPrompts.example: My grandfather cannot walk fast, so we will walk slowly with him.

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. Where did they arrive when the sun rose?
beforeYouRead.quote: When the sun rose, they arrived at the sea.

iCan: I can tell about the night journey.
I can say what we must do.
I can plan a safe trip.

pages.title: The Sea Opens
pages.content: Moses (pbuh) and his people saw the king and his soldiers following them. His people panicked. But Moses (pbuh) said, “Calm down! Allah is with us and will help us go to a safe place.” Soon, the king and his soldiers caught up with them! The sea was in front of them. The king and his army were behind them. They had no place to escape. But Allah was with them. He told Moses (pbuh), “Hit the sea with your stick!” He hit the sea and the sea parted! The waves became high walls! They could see the sandy ground! Allah made a road in the sea for them. Moses (pbuh) and his people safely walked between the walls of water.

vocabulary.definition: Felt sudden, strong fear.
Reached someone who was ahead.
Opened and moved to two sides.
Tall, straight sides that stop people from passing.

hotspots.title: The Stick and the Sea
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) hit the sea with his stick, and the sea parted.

hotspots.title: Walls of Water
hotspots.description: Moses (pbuh) and his people walked safely between walls of water.

exercises.title: Calm in Danger
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 15.
exercises.question: Moses’s people panicked. What did Moses (pbuh) say to them?
options: “Get ready for the journey. … We will leave at night.”
“Calm down! Allah is with us and will help us go to a safe place.”
“Wait here. I will get some fire to get warm.”
exercises.explanation: At the beginning of Chapter 15, Moses said, “Calm down! Allah is with us and will help us go to a safe place.” Then Allah told him to hit the sea with his stick, and the sea parted.

feedback.correct: Yes! Moses trusted Allah and helped his frightened people stay calm.
feedback.incorrect: Read the beginning of Chapter 15 again. Find what Moses said right after his people panicked.

languageFocusExercises.title: In Front Of, Behind, With
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. One word is not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where were the sea and the army?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: The sea was [blank] them. The king and his army were [blank] them. They had no place to escape. But Allah was [blank] them.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: In front of and behind show position: The sea was ahead, and the army was at their back. With shows that Allah was helping them.

feedback.correct: Correct. The sea in front, the army behind, and Allah with them.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 15 again. Where was the sea? Where did the army come from?

languageFocusExercises.title: The Sea Opens
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the sentences from Chapter 15 in story order.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened after Moses hit the sea?

sequencingItems.text: Moses hit the sea and the sea parted!
The waves became high walls!
Moses and his people could see the sandy ground!
Moses (pbuh) and his people safely walked between the walls of water.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Became shows a change (waves → walls). Could see shows what was now possible. Safely walked between tells us how and where they moved.

feedback.correct: Correct. From the first change to the safe walk.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 15 again. Start with Moses hitting the sea.

languageFocusExercises.title: Fix the Verbs
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct word.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the two verbs?

errorItems.sentence: “Calm down! Allah … will helps us go to a safe place.”
Soon, the king and his soldiers catched up with them!

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After will, use the base verb with no -s: will help. Catch is irregular: catch → caught. Catch up with means reach someone who is in front of you.

feedback.correct: Well done. Will help and caught up with.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 15 again. After will, the verb does not change. Catch has an irregular past.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: Find a Safe Route
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about a busy street.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you find a safe way through a busy place?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use in front of, behind, an imperative, will, became, could, between and safely.

feedback.correct: Use a new everyday route.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say what is in front and behind: “… was in front of us, and … was behind us.”
discussionPrompts.example: The big market was in front of us, and the bus station was behind us.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Help someone feel calm: “Calm down! … We will …”
discussionPrompts.example: Calm down! Hold my hand. We will find the way.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say how something changed: “The … became …”
discussionPrompts.example: The busy street became quiet after six o’clock.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say the safe way: “We walked between …”
discussionPrompts.example: We walked between the fruit shops to the park.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Who was behind Moses’s people?
beforeYouRead.quote: The king and his army were behind them.

iCan: I can tell how the sea opened.
I can say what is in front of me and behind me.
I can describe a safe way through a busy place.

pages.title: The Cruel King Died in the Water
pages.content: The king and his soldiers were very close behind them. They also saw the road in the middle of the sea. The king said to his soldiers, “Look! I told the sea to open, and it opened.” They entered the waters. When they were midway, Allah closed the sea over them. In the end, they died in the water. The story of Moses (pbuh) has many lessons to learn. It tells us that no one can own another person. It shows that only Allah has power over us.

vocabulary.definition: Halfway between the start and the end.
Things we learn from a story or event.
To have something that belongs to you.
The ability to control people or things.

hotspots.title: The Closed Sea
hotspots.description: When the king and his soldiers were midway, Allah closed the sea over them.

hotspots.title: Only Allah
hotspots.description: No one can own another person. Only Allah has power over people.

exercises.title: Who Opened the Sea?
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 16.
exercises.question: When the king saw the road in the sea, he said that Allah opened it.
exercises.explanation: The king said, “Look! I told the sea to open, and it opened.” But Allah made the road for Moses and his people, and Allah closed the sea over the king’s army. The story ends: “It shows that only Allah has power over us.”

feedback.correct: Correct! The king said that he opened the sea. The ending shows that only Allah has this power.
feedback.incorrect: Read the beginning of Chapter 16 again. What did the king say to his soldiers?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Do These Sentences Give Us?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the end of Chapter 16. Choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “It tells us that no one can own another person. It shows that only Allah has power over us.” What do these two sentences give us?
options: a new event in the story
languageFocusExercises.explanation: It tells us that … and It shows that … introduce a lesson. The present simple (tells, shows, has) is used because a lesson is always true, not only in the past.

feedback.correct: Correct. These sentences give lessons from the story.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last lines of Chapter 16. The sentence before them says the story “has many lessons to learn”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Said To, Told … To
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix what the king said?

errorItems.sentence: “Look! I told the sea open, and it opened.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Say to + person: Said to his soldiers. Tell + person/thing + to + base verb: told the sea to open. We do not say told to the sea.

feedback.correct: Well done. Said to his soldiers, and told the sea to open.
feedback.incorrect: Read the king’s words in Chapter 16 again. Said needs to before the person; told needs to before the verb.

languageFocusExercises.title: Place and Time Words
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each word from Chapter 16 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these words from Chapter 16 mean?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Very close behind tells us where. When they were midway and In the end tell us when: In the end introduces the final result.

feedback.correct: Correct. You know the place and time words of the final scene.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 16 again. Find each word and look at the sentence around it.

languageFocusExercises.title: Use It: Explain a Simple Lesson
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say four short sentences about a small job you did together.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened, and what does it teach us?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use in the middle of, when, in the end, said to/told + person + to, It tells us that, or It shows that.

feedback.correct: Use a new everyday story.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say where and when: “Last …, we were at …”
discussionPrompts.example: Last Saturday, we were at the library.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say what someone told you to do: “… told us to …”
discussionPrompts.example: The librarian told us to put the books back on the shelves.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say how it ended: “In the end, …”
discussionPrompts.example: In the end, the shelves were tidy again.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Give the lesson: “This story tells us that …”
discussionPrompts.example: This story tells us that small jobs help everyone.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did Allah do to the sea?
options: He closed it over the king’s army.
beforeYouRead.quote: When they were midway, Allah closed the sea over them.

iCan: I can tell how the cruel king’s story ended.
I can say what happened in the end.
I can say one lesson from a story.

groupTask.title: Helpers in the Story

roles.name: Quote Finder
roles.job: You copy one sentence about each helper from Chapters 3–9 exactly.

roles.name: Writer
roles.job: You write two sentences about a helper in your school or family.

roles.name: Language Checker
roles.job: You check that the poster uses two patterns, like “told … to …” or “because …”.

roles.name: Designer
roles.job: You put the words on the poster in a clear way. Use words only, with no pictures of people.

steps: Choose three helpers from Chapters 3–9, for example Moses’s sister, Queen Asiye or the young man at the well.
For each helper, copy one sentence from the book, for example: “He was always ready to help the weak people.” or “told her daughter to follow the basket”.
Write two sentences about a helper in your school or family: “My … always … because …”.
Practise and present your poster in two minutes.

legend.route:exodus: The night journey to the sea

places.name: Egypt
places.text: Moses (pbuh) lived in Egypt more than 3000 years ago. Pharaoh was the king of Egypt. The king’s palace and the city were here. The Children of Israel lived here too.
places.teacherNote: The A2 text does not name the city or say where the palace was. Show Egypt as a region, not as one exact place.
places.question: Who was the king of Egypt? Was he kind or cruel?

places.name: The River Nile
places.text: Moses’s mother put her baby in a basket. She put the basket on the River Nile. The water carried it to the edge of the river near the king’s palace.
places.teacherNote: The text does not say where on the Nile this happened. The soft area shows the river in Egypt, not an exact place. The Arabic edition says “a small box” (tābūt) instead of a basket.
places.question: Who followed the basket? Why?

places.name: Midian
places.text: Moses left Egypt and traveled for many days to Midian. The king of Egypt was not the ruler there. At a well, Moses helped two sisters with their sheep. He lived in Midian for ten years.
places.teacherNote: The A2 text says only that Midian was near Egypt. The B1 and B2 books say it was on the eastern side of the Gulf of Aqaba. The place of the well is not known.
places.question: Why did Moses go to Midian? Who did he meet there?

places.name: The Mountain
places.text: After ten years, Moses and his family traveled back to Egypt. It was winter. In a valley between mountains, Moses saw a fire. He climbed the mountain and heard the voice of Allah.
places.teacherNote: The A2 text does not name this mountain. The B2 book calls it Mount Sinai, also known as Mount Tur. The soft area in the south of the Sinai Peninsula is approximate; the exact place is not known.
places.question: What did Allah tell Moses to do with his walking stick?

places.name: The Sea
places.text: Moses (pbuh) and his people left Egypt at night. When the sun rose, they arrived at the sea. Moses hit the sea with his stick and the sea parted. The king and his soldiers died in the water.
places.teacherNote: The A2 text does not name the sea. The B1 and B2 books call it the Red Sea. The exact place of the crossing is not known; the soft area at the Gulf of Suez is approximate.
places.question: How did Allah help Moses and his people at the sea?
