pages.title: Knowledge Check
pages.content: Test your understanding of the story of Moses (pbuh).

exercises.title: The Children of Israel
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Why did the Children of Israel not think the king was a god?
options: They were afraid of the king.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “They believed in one Allah, like Prophet Abraham (pbuh). So, they did not think the king was a god.”

feedback.correct: Yes! Like Prophet Abraham, they believed in one Allah, so the king could not be their god.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the middle of Chapter 1 again. What did the Children of Israel believe?

exercises.title: The King’s Dream
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: In the king’s dream, the fire burnt the houses of the Egyptians.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “The fire came from Jerusalem and burnt the houses of the Egyptians. But it did not harm any of the Children of Israel.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is true. The fire burnt the houses of the Egyptians, but it did not harm the Children of Israel.
feedback.incorrect: Read the dream in Chapter 2 again. Whose houses did the fire burn?

exercises.title: A Worried Mother
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Why could Moses’s mother not sleep at night?
options: She was afraid the soldiers could find her baby.
Her baby was hungry and was crying all night.
She had to work in the king’s palace in the morning.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “His mother was afraid that soldiers could find her baby. So, she could not sleep at night.”

feedback.correct: Yes. The soldiers were killing baby boys, so she was very afraid for Moses.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the first sentences of Chapter 3 again. What was his mother afraid of?

exercises.title: In the King’s House
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: Moses grew up in the king’s house, but he knew the king was not a god.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “Moses grew up in a safe place, in the house of the king. He always loved Allah. He knew that the king was not a god.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is true. He lived in the palace, but he always loved Allah.
feedback.incorrect: Read the middle of Chapter 5 again. What did Moses know about the king?

exercises.title: The Way to Midian
exercises.instructions: Read the sentence. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: Moses traveled to Midian all alone, without any help.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “He left Egypt and traveled for a long time. He was not alone. Allah guided him.”

feedback.correct: Right, it is false. The story says he was not alone: Allah guided him.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first lines of Chapter 7 again. Was Moses really alone?

exercises.title: The Voice
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: What did Moses hear first in the silence on the mountain?
options: “Moses, I am Allah. I chose you.”
exercises.explanation: Chapter 10: “In the silence, he heard a loud voice: “Moses, I am Allah. I chose you. Listen to me. There is no god but Me.””

feedback.correct: Yes! Allah spoke to Moses and told him that He chose him.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the end of Chapter 10 again. What did the loud voice say first?

exercises.title: The King Listens
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Moses said, “I am the Messenger from the Lord of the universe.” What did the king think?
options: He thought Moses was a king.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 12: “The king listened to Moses (pbuh). He thought Moses was crazy.”

feedback.correct: Yes. The king did not believe Moses. He thought Moses was crazy, so Moses showed the miracles.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the first lines of Chapter 12 again. What did the king think after he listened?

exercises.title: A Hard Life
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer.
exercises.question: Life became harder for Moses’s people. What did Moses do?
options: He went to live in Midian again.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 14: “Life became harder for them. Moses (pbuh) asked Allah for help. And Allah told him, “Travel with your people at night.””

feedback.correct: Yes. Moses asked Allah for help, and Allah told him to travel with his people at night.
feedback.incorrect: Not this one. Read the start of Chapter 14 again. Who did Moses ask for help?

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review and use the grammar patterns and language functions from all sixteen chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Was It Happening or Did It Happen?
exercises.instructions: Was it already happening, or finished? Put each sentence in a group.
exercises.question: What is the difference between “was walking” and “saw”?

items: One day Moses was walking in the bazaar.
They were watering their animals.
The king was sitting on his throne.
Moses saw two men fighting.
Soon, he found a well.
Moses met the king and his helpers.

Already happening at that moment: One day Moses was walking in the bazaar.
The king was sitting on his throne.
A finished action: Moses met the king and his helpers.

exercises.explanation: Was/were + verb-ing (was walking, were watering, was sitting) shows an action that was already happening at that moment. It paints the background of the scene. The past simple (saw, found, met) tells a finished action, often a new event in that scene: Moses was walking, and then he saw two men.

feedback.correct: Well done. Was/were + -ing is the background; the past simple is the event.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verb. Does it have was/were + -ing, or is it one past verb (saw, found, met)?

exercises.title: Look: Able or Not Able?
exercises.instructions: Match each sentence from the book with its meaning.
exercises.question: What do can, cannot, could and could not mean?

matchingPairs.left: All of my magicians can do this.
Moses and his people could see the sandy ground!
matchingPairs.right: They were able then, in the past.

matchingPairs.left: The children and the old could not walk fast …
matchingPairs.right: They were not able then, in the past.

correctAnswer.Moses and his people could see the sandy: They were able then, in the past.
correctAnswer.The children and the old could not walk: They were not able then, in the past.

exercises.explanation: Can + base verb means able now, and cannot + base verb means not able now. The girls and the king are speaking, so they use can and cannot. Could and could not are the past: The story tells us what people were able or not able to do at that time. After can, cannot, could and could not, use the base verb without “to”.

feedback.correct: Correct. Can and cannot are about now; could and could not are about the past.
feedback.incorrect: Ask two questions for each sentence: Able or not able? Now or in the past?

exercises.title: Look: Will and Going To
exercises.instructions: Read the three speakers’ words. Then choose the best answer.
exercises.question: The helpers and magicians: “A boy will be born from the Children of Israel …” The man from the city: “Now they are going to catch you.” Moses (pbuh): “We will leave at night.” When do these actions happen?
options: at the same moment as the person speaks
exercises.explanation: Will + base verb and are going to + base verb talk about the future. The helpers and magicians make a prediction (will be born), the man from the city says what he expects soon (are going to catch), and Moses gives a plan (will leave). After that, the story tells what really happened in the past: “They left Egypt at night.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Will and going to look forward to the future.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the verbs: will be born, are going to catch, will leave. Has the action happened yet?

exercises.title: Practise: Reason, Result, Different Idea
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
exercises.question: Which word fits each gap?
exercises.fillBlanksText: [blank] his fear, he was rude to the Children of Israel. … Moses’s mother was so sad. [blank] she knew that Allah was kinder to the baby Moses than she was. … He was so sorry [blank] he accidentally caused someone’s death. … He was very old, [blank] he couldn’t help his daughters.
exercises.explanation: “Because of” + a noun gives a reason: because of his fear. “Because” + a sentence also gives a reason: because he accidentally caused someone’s death. “So” gives the result: He was very old, so he couldn’t help. “But” gives a different idea: She was sad, but she knew Allah was kinder to her baby.

feedback.correct: Well done. You linked reasons, results and a different idea.
feedback.incorrect: For each gap, ask: Is the next part a reason, a result or a different idea? Is there a noun or a whole sentence after the gap?

exercises.title: Practise: What Comes After the Verb?
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence from the book.
exercises.question: What comes after “forced them”, “began” and “gave them to Moses”?

formChoices.sentence: He forced them [choice] dangerous work for no money.
Moses began [choice] with the family.
Allah gave them to Moses (pbuh) [choice] him.

exercises.explanation: Force + person + to + verb: “forced them to do”. Begin + to + verb: “began to stay”. To + verb can also answer the question “Why?”: Allah gave the miracles to Moses to help him. We do not say for help him.

feedback.correct: Correct. Forced them to …, began to …, and to + verb for a purpose.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the word before the gap: forced them, began, gave them … . Which form has “to”?

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Past Verb
exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap it, then choose the correct words.
exercises.question: Can you fix the verb in each sentence?

errorItems.sentence: When the sun rised, they arrived at the sea.
His helpers and soldiers was standing around him.

exercises.explanation: “Think” and “rise” are irregular: think → thought, rise → rose (not thinked, rised). “Raised” is a different verb. His helpers and soldiers are more than one person, so we use were + verb-ing: were standing.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed all three sentences.
feedback.incorrect: Compare with the book: The king’s opinion in Chapter 12, the morning in Chapter 14 and the palace scene at the end of Chapter 11.

exercises.title: Practise: The Queen’s Decision
exercises.instructions: Put the words in order to make the queen’s words.
exercises.question: How does the queen say her decision?
exercises.explanation: I will + base verb shows a decision: the queen decides at that moment. After “and”, the second verb is also a base verb, and we do not need to say will again: will take him … and look after him.

feedback.correct: Well done. I will + verb … and + verb shows her decision.
feedback.incorrect: Start with “I will”. What will she do first, and where? Then add the second action with “and”.

exercises.title: Use: A Rainy Morning
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps in this new text. Two words are not needed.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s words in a rainy-day story?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Last Monday, I [blank] walking to school with my little brother. It was cold and rainy, [blank] we walked fast. My brother could not find his hat. I gave him my scarf [blank] keep him warm. He smiled and said, “Tomorrow I [blank] bring my own hat.”
exercises.explanation: “I was walking” shows the background: The action was happening at that time. “So” gives the result of the cold rain. “To keep him warm” says why. “I will bring” is a promise for tomorrow. Like Moses at the well, the writer sees a need and helps.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s language in a new place.
feedback.incorrect: Ask for each gap: Background or event? reason or result? why? now or tomorrow?

exercises.title: Use: A Time Someone Needed Help
exercises.instructions: Write 4–5 sentences about helping someone. Tell a partner first.
exercises.question: Can you tell a short story from your life?
exercises.explanation: Example: “Last week, I was waiting for the bus with my mother. An old man was standing near us. His bag was very heavy, so he could not carry it. My mother told me to help him. I carried his bag to the bus. Next time, I will help again because it is the right thing to do.”

feedback.correct: Check your sentences: was/were + -ing, a past verb, could not, because or so, told … to …, will.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Set the scene: “Last …, I was …-ing …”
discussionPrompts.example: Last winter, I was walking home from school with my friend.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say the problem: “He/She could not … because …”
discussionPrompts.example: An old man could not carry his shopping bags because they were very heavy.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say how you helped: “My … told me to … . I decided to …”
discussionPrompts.example: My friend told me to help him, so I decided to carry the bags to his door.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what you will do: “Next time, I will …”
discussionPrompts.example: Next time, I will help him again.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Test your knowledge of the entire story of Prophet Moses (pbuh).

exercises.title: A Mother’s Trust
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 3 with one word: kinder, closer or stronger.
exercises.question: What did Moses’s mother know about Allah?
exercises.fillBlanksText: But she knew that Allah was [blank] to the baby Moses than she was.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3 says: “Moses’s mother was so sad. But she knew that Allah was kinder to the baby Moses than she was.”

feedback.correct: Yes. She was sad, but she trusted Allah with her baby.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 3. She was sad, but what did she know about Allah?

exercises.title: At the Well
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.question: Why were the two girls sitting far from the well?
options: They were waiting for their turn.
Their sheep did not want to drink.
exercises.explanation: In Chapter 8 the girls say: “Our father is very old. He cannot come with us. There are no young men in our house to help us. So, we take the sheep to the water. We wait for our turn.”

feedback.correct: Yes. They had no one to help them, so they waited for the other shepherds.
feedback.incorrect: Read what the girls say to Moses at the start of Chapter 8.

exercises.title: The Girls’ Father
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.question: Who was the father of the two sisters?
options: a rich shepherd from the land of Egypt
a Messenger of Allah in Midian
one of the king’s helpers in Egypt
exercises.explanation: Chapter 9 says: “The father of these girls was Prophet Shu’ayb (pbuh). Shu’ayb (pbuh) was a Messenger of Allah in Midian.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Moses found a new home with a prophet’s family.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first sentences of Chapter 9.

exercises.title: Who Said It?
exercises.instructions: Match each person with their words.
exercises.question: Who said these words in the story?

matchingPairs.right: “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!”

correctAnswer.the magicians: “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!”

exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: a man from the city says, “Run away from the city.” Chapter 9: Shu’ayb says, “Go and call the young man. I want to thank him for his work.” Chapter 12: the king says, “This is only magic. All of my magicians can do this.” Chapter 13: the magicians shout, “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!”

feedback.correct: Yes. Their words show who helped Moses and who did not believe.
feedback.incorrect: Look again at Chapters 6, 9, 12 and 13. Who is speaking there?

exercises.title: The King Does Not Change
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.question: The magicians believed in Allah. Why did the king still not believe?
options: His magicians told him not to.
He did not see Moses’s stick.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 13 says: “The king still did not believe in Allah because he was arrogant.” He even continued “to harm Moses (pbuh) and his people day and night.”

feedback.correct: Yes. He saw the same miracle as the magicians, but his pride stopped him.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 13. Find the word “because”.

exercises.title: A Secret Journey
exercises.instructions: Decide whether the sentence is true or false.
exercises.question: Moses told his people to keep the journey a secret.
exercises.explanation: In Chapter 14 Moses says: “But you must keep it secret. We must hide it. We will leave at night.”

feedback.correct: True. They left at night, and nobody was to know.
feedback.incorrect: Read what Moses says to his people in Chapter 14.

exercises.title: Allah’s Help
exercises.instructions: Match each thing with what happened to it.
exercises.question: How did Allah help Moses in the story?

matchingPairs.right: The waves carried it near the palace.
It turned into a big snake.

correctAnswer.the basket: The waves carried it near the palace.
correctAnswer.the walking stick: It turned into a big snake.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “Soon, the basket came to the edge of the river. It was near the king’s palace.” Chapter 12: “The stick turned into a big snake!” and “He took his hand out. Look! It was shining white!” Chapter 15: “He hit the sea and the sea parted! The waves became high walls!”

feedback.correct: Yes. Allah helped Moses from the day he was a baby.
feedback.incorrect: Look again at Chapters 4, 12 and 15.

exercises.title: A Way Through the Sea
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 15 with one word: road, house or boat.
exercises.question: What did Allah make for Moses and his people?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Allah made a [blank] in the sea for them.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 15 says: “Allah made a road in the sea for them. Moses (pbuh) and his people safely walked between the walls of water.”

feedback.correct: Yes. They walked on dry sand between the walls of water.
feedback.incorrect: Read the end of Chapter 15. How did the people cross the sea?

exercises.title: The Last Lesson
exercises.instructions: Decide whether the sentence is true or false.
exercises.question: At the end, the story says that no one can own another person.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 16 says: “It tells us that no one can own another person. It shows that only Allah has power over us.”

feedback.correct: Right. The king thought he owned the people, but only Allah has power over us.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last two sentences of the story.

exercises.title: Moses’s Life
exercises.instructions: Put the events in the correct order.
exercises.question: What happened first, next and later in Moses’s life?

sequencingItems.text: Moses helps two sisters water their sheep.
The king tells his soldiers to kill the baby boys.
Moses and his people leave Egypt at night.
Moses’s sister brings her mother to the palace.
Moses hears a voice on the mountain.

exercises.explanation: The king’s order (Chapter 2), the mother in the palace (Chapter 5), the well in Midian (Chapter 8), the voice on the mountain (Chapter 10) and the night journey (Chapter 14).

feedback.correct: Yes. Moses goes from the palace to Midian and back to Egypt.
feedback.incorrect: Remember: Moses was a baby in Egypt, then he lived in Midian, then he came back.
